deepFindings: Chrome's official extension testing guidance explicitly treats forced service-worker termination as a correctness test and uses CDP target discovery/close; this is the strongest next Ferrum extension experiment because it adds failure-injection coverage without a new framework.

ProcDump-for-Linux recently added programmatic dump access plus ARM and stack-overflow fixes, making a failure-only crash-evidence adapter more practical, but it remains secondary to the service-worker experiment because Ferrum has a direct untested MV3 resilience gap today.
rr and gVisor are powerful but too environment-heavy for Ferrum's default acceptance lane; retain them as opt-in research paths rather than trading fidelity or startup cost for theoretical coverage.
nextExperiments: Implement an isolated Chromium-only terminate-service-worker action using the existing CDP connection, then prove the exact self-test MV3 worker is closed and reactivated by a fresh popup message on Linux and Windows while existing full-browser restart proof still passes.

After MV3 termination is proven, prototype one failure-only Linux crash-capture experiment comparing ordinary Ferrum logs against ProcDump metadata/core evidence; keep it optional unless the additional evidence is actionable and bounded.
Evaluate bubblewrap only on a self-contained process fixture and reject it if isolation changes behavior or creates measurable setup cost without a real project need.
guardrails: Do not replace Playwright or Ferrum's qualified browser lifecycle for one CDP operation; use the narrowest exact-target helper.
Do not terminate arbitrary service workers, background targets, pages, or browser processes; exact extension identity is mandatory.
Crash/sandbox tooling must be failure-only or opt-in unless repeated before/after evidence proves acceptable overhead and unchanged target fidelity.
No existing Linux, Windows, browser-matrix, MV3 restart, Spaces, Workbench, packaged desktop, Lightpanda, Selenium Grid, Appium, MCP or evidence gate may be weakened.
researchCursorNext: forced-MV3-worker-recovery implementation; then crash-dump evidence and lightweight process isolation
